mainTopic: What makes a fast a real תענית: lasting until sunset, accepting it in advance, and eating the night before
overview: רב חסדא teaches that 'fasting for hours' counts only if nothing is eaten until evening. This covers someone who decided partway through the day to keep fasting. He also rules that a fast broken before sunset is not called a תענית. Three challenges, from the אנשי משמר, the family of סנאה בן בנימין, and רבי יוחנן, are each answered: none of those cases was a real תענית. שמואל adds that a fast must be accepted while it is still day, and someone who fasts without accepting it is like a bellows full of air. רב and שמואל argue whether the acceptance happens in the afternoon or during the מנחה prayer. רב יוסף tries to prove שמואל's view from מגילת תענית, but the proof is pushed away by reading יאסר instead of ייסר, and the גמרא explains that reading. Finally, a ברייתא discusses how late one may eat the night before a fast. אביי and רבא limit that permission by finishing the meal or by sleep. The amud ends as רב אשי begins to define 'dozing'.

steps.title: Fasting for hours only counts if nothing is eaten until evening
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא qualifies the rule of מתענין לשעות: it applies only if the person tasted nothing until nightfall.
steps.simpleTranslation: That rule you mentioned, that a person may fast for a few hours, only applies if he didn't eat anything until evening.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא adds a condition to the earlier rule that a person can take on a fast 'for hours.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: A fast 'for hours' does not mean eating in the morning, stopping for a bit, and then eating again. It means the person ate nothing at all until evening. Accepting a few hours of fasting is fine, but only if those hours run all the way to nightfall.

phrases.english: That which you said, 'one may fast for hours' —

phrases.aramaic: וְהוּא שֶׁלֹּא טָעַם כְּלוּם עַד הָעֶרֶב.
phrases.english: that is only where he did not taste anything until the evening.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the discussion of fasting for hours from the previous daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A fast 'for hours' counts only if the person ate nothing until evening.

steps.title: אביי: that is just a full fast
steps.stepSummary: אביי objects that if the person ate nothing all day, this is simply a full תענית, so the rule seems obvious.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: But that is a complete fast!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי challenges רב חסדא: if the person didn't eat all day, why call it a 'fast for hours'? It is a regular full-day fast.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the condition is 'nothing eaten until evening,' the person fasted the entire day. So the special category of 'fasting for hours' seems to add nothing.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
But this is a full-fledged fast!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for the qualification in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's condition that nothing be eaten until evening
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If no food was eaten all day, it is an ordinary full fast, so the rule says nothing new.

steps.title: The case: he decided to fast partway through the day
steps.stepSummary: The rule is needed for someone who did not plan to fast in the morning but decided midday to keep fasting until night.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, the rule is needed where he changed his mind partway through the day.
steps.whatsHappening: The answer explains what the rule adds: a person who hadn't eaten and then decided in the middle of the day to fast until evening.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A 'full fast' is planned from the start of the day. Here the person ate nothing but only accepted the fast later, for the remaining hours. רב חסדא teaches that this still counts as a תענית.

keyTerms.meaning: it is only needed for (a specific case)
he changed his mind / decided later

phrases.english: No, it is needed —
where he changed his mind.
phrases.notes: He started the day with no plan to fast, didn't happen to eat, and then decided to keep fasting until night.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The rule seemed to describe an ordinary full-day fast.
steps.terutzMaskana: It describes someone who accepted the fast midday, and that still counts as a תענית.
steps.whatToRemember: 'Fasting for hours' means accepting a fast partway through the day, as long as nothing is eaten until nightfall.

steps.title: A fast that ends before sunset is not a fast
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא rules that any fast the sun does not set on is not called a תענית.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב חסדא said: Any fast that the sun doesn't set on is not called a fast.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא makes a new, related statement: a fast must last until sunset to be a real תענית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This states directly what step 1 implied. If you stop fasting and eat before sunset, what you did does not have the status of a תענית at all. The rest of this section challenges this ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: it is not called a fast

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the main rule tested by the next three challenges.

phrases.english: And Rav Ḥisda said:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל תַּעֲנִית שֶׁלֹּא שָׁקְעָה עָלָיו חַמָּה —
phrases.english: Any fast upon which the sun did not set —
is not called a fast.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, related ruling from the same אמורא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A fast that is broken before sunset is not a תענית.

steps.title: Challenge from the אנשי משמר, who fast but do not finish
steps.stepSummary: A משנה says the אנשי משמר fast without completing the day, which suggests a partial fast is still called a fast.
steps.simpleTranslation: An objection: the members of the משמר fast, but they don't finish the fast!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב חסדא with a source saying the אנשי משמר 'fast' even though they stop before evening.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The source uses the word 'fast' for something that doesn't last until sunset. That seems to contradict רב חסדא's rule that such a fast is not called a תענית.

keyTerms.meaning: the כהנים on duty in the בית המקדש that week

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
The members of the priestly watch fast but do not complete it!
phrases.notes: These are the כהנים serving in the בית המקדש that week.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב חסדא's ruling in step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's rule that a fast without sunset is not a fast
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The source calls a partial-day fast a 'fast.'

steps.title: That was only self-affliction
steps.stepSummary: The אנשי משמר were not keeping a real תענית; they held back from food only to share in the community's distress.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, it was just to cause themselves distress.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב חסדא: the אנשי משמר's fasting was not an official תענית, only an act of personal self-affliction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The source uses the word 'fast' loosely. The כהנים felt the community's pain and held back from eating for part of the day, but it did not have the legal status of a תענית. So רב חסדא's rule stands.

phrases.english: There, it is merely to cause themselves distress.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection in step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case as non-fast self-affliction
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The אנשי משמר kept a real partial-day תענית.
steps.terutzMaskana: It was only a show of distress, not a legal תענית.

steps.title: Challenge from the family of סנאה בן בנימין on a delayed תשעה באב
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר ברבי צדוק says his family fasted on the postponed תשעה באב but did not complete it, because that day was their family יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רבי אלעזר ברבי צדוק said, 'I am a descendant of סנאה בן בנימין. Once תשעה באב fell on שבת, and we pushed it off to after שבת. We fasted on it but did not finish, because it is our own יום טוב.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second source against רב חסדא: a family that kept a partial fast on the postponed תשעה באב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story describes this partial fast with the language of fasting. That seems to show that a fast broken before sunset is still a תענית.

phrases.aramaic: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי צָדוֹק:
phrases.english: Come and hear, as Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Tzadok said:

phrases.aramaic: אֲנִי מִבְּנֵי בָנָיו שֶׁל סְנָאָה בֶּן בִּנְיָמִין,
phrases.english: I am a descendant of Senaah of the tribe of Benjamin,

phrases.aramaic: וּפַעַם אַחַת חָל תִּשְׁעָה בְּאָב לִהְיוֹת בְּשַׁבָּת,
phrases.english: and once the Ninth of Av fell on Shabbat,
and we postponed it until after Shabbat,
and we fasted on it but did not complete it —
because it is a holiday of ours.
phrases.notes: The postponed fast landed on the tenth of אב, which was this family's own special day.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי צָדוֹק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second challenge to רב חסדא, after the first was answered.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A partial fast is described as a fast, so it seems to count.

steps.title: That too was only self-affliction
steps.stepSummary: The family's partial fast was also just an act of distress, not a legal תענית.
steps.simpleTranslation: There too, it was just to cause themselves distress.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the same answer as before: the family was only showing distress, not keeping a real fast.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the day was their יום טוב, they could not truly fast, but they still held back for part of the day to mourn. That is self-affliction, not a תענית, so רב חסדא is not contradicted.

phrases.aramaic: הָתָם נָמֵי, לְצַעוֹרֵי נַפְשֵׁיהּ בְּעָלְמָא הוּא.
phrases.english: There too, it is merely to cause themselves distress.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם נָמֵי, לְצַעוֹרֵי נַפְשֵׁיהּ בְּעָלְמָא הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reuses the answer from step 6 for the new challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case as non-fast self-affliction
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The family kept a real partial-day תענית.
steps.terutzMaskana: It was only an act of distress, not a legal תענית.

steps.title: Challenge from רבי יוחנן's fast until he got home
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן used to say he would fast until he reached his house, which suggests one can take on a short fast.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רבי יוחנן said, 'I will be fasting until I get to my house.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a third challenge: רבי יוחנן took on a fast that lasted only until he got home.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here a great אמורא speaks of a fast lasting just a few hours, and he would eat once he got home, before evening. That seems to show a partial fast counts as a תענית.

keyTerms.meaning: I shall be in a fast

phrases.english: Come and hear, as Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
I shall be fasting until I come to my house.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third challenge to רב חסדא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן accepted a fast of only a few hours, which implies it is a real תענית.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן was politely excusing himself from the נשיא's house
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן's 'fast' was only a polite way to turn down eating at the house of the נשיא, not a real תענית.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, he did it to get himself out of the נשיא's house.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי יוחנן wasn't really fasting. He was giving a polite excuse not to stay and eat with the נשיא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'I'm fasting' let him decline the invitation without insulting the נשיא, and then he ate at home. Since it was an excuse and not a real fast, it does not prove that a partial fast is a תענית. רב חסדא's rule survives all three challenges.
steps.whatToRemember: All three challenges fail for the same reason: none of the cases was a true תענית. So רב חסדא's rule stands: a fast broken before sunset is not called a fast.

phrases.english: There, it was to excuse himself
from the house of the Nasi that he did it.
phrases.notes: He wanted a polite way to turn down a meal at the נשיא's house without giving offense.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם, לְשַׁמּוֹטֵי נַפְשֵׁיהּ מִבֵּי נְשִׂיאָה הוּא דַּעֲבַד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reframing the act as an excuse rather than a fast
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוחנן kept a real fast that lasted only a few hours.
steps.terutzMaskana: His 'fast' was a polite excuse, not a legal תענית.

steps.title: A fast must be accepted the day before
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules that a fast not accepted while it was still day is not called a fast.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: any fast that a person did not take upon himself while it was still daytime is not called a fast.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new rule from שמואל: a תענית only counts if you accepted it beforehand, while it was still day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a separate requirement from רב חסדא's rule about lasting until sunset. שמואל adds a formal condition: a real תענית needs an acceptance (קבלה) made in advance, while it is still daytime on the day before. Not eating without that acceptance does not create a legal fast.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not called (it does not count as)

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the הלכה that a voluntary fast must be accepted ahead of time.

phrases.english: Shmuel said:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל תַּעֲנִית שֶׁלֹּא קִיבֵּל עָלָיו מִבְּעוֹד יוֹם —
phrases.english: Any fast that he did not take upon himself while it was still day —
phrases.notes: He means daytime on the day before the fast.

phrases.english: is not called a fast.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: כׇּל תַּעֲנִית שֶׁלֹּא קִיבֵּל עָלָיו מִבְּעוֹד יוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new rule about accepting a fast, after the earlier steps showed that various partial fasts were not real fasts.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A fast that was not accepted while it was still day is not a legal תענית.

steps.title: What if he fasted anyway?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what it means if someone sat and fasted without accepting the fast in advance.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if he sat in a fast anyway, what is he?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a follow-up question about שמואל's rule. It is setting up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל said such a day is 'not called a fast'. So what is it when someone goes without food all day anyway? The גמרא wants to know how to describe that person.

keyTerms.meaning: Sits (here: sits in a fast, goes without eating)

phrases.english: And if he sat [fasting], what is he?
phrases.notes: He means: if he went without food all day without accepting the fast first.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the status of someone who fasts without the acceptance שמואל required.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the status of someone who went without food without accepting a fast in advance?

steps.title: Like a bellows full of air
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר שילא answers that such a person is like a bellows filled with air.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר שילא said: he is like a bellows that is full of air.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר שילא answers the question with a picture: this person is just like a bellows full of air.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A bellows has nothing real inside, only air. In the same way, this person is empty of food but has no real fast, so he gets no credit for a תענית. He suffered hunger for nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: A bellows (a tool that blows air)

phrases.english: Rabba bar Sheila said:
He is like a bellows that is full of air.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר שֵׁילָא: דָּמֵי לְמַפּוּחָא דְּמַלְיָא זִיקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He is like an empty bellows full of air. He went hungry, but it is not a fast at all.

steps.title: When is the fast accepted?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks at what time a person accepts a fast upon himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: When does he accept it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a new practical question: at what point on the day before does a person accept the fast? It is setting up an argument in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל only said 'while it is still day'. That is a long stretch of time, so the גמרא wants to know exactly when the acceptance happens.

phrases.english: When does he accept it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows שמואל's 'while it is still day' to an exact time.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: At what time on the day before is the fast accepted?

steps.title: רב and שמואל argue about the time
steps.stepSummary: רב says the fast is accepted in the afternoon (במנחה). שמואל says it is accepted during the מנחה prayer.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: in the afternoon. שמואל said: in the מנחה prayer.
steps.whatsHappening: Two answers are given. רב says any time in the afternoon works, and שמואל says it must be done during the מנחה prayer itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב, 'מנחה' means the time of day, the afternoon. For שמואל, 'תפלת המנחה' means the prayer itself, so the acceptance is tied to davening מנחה.
steps.confusionAlert: The two answers sound almost the same. Watch the difference: רב means the time of day, while שמואל means the actual מנחה prayer.

phrases.english: Rav said: in the afternoon,
phrases.notes: He means the afternoon time of the day before the fast.

phrases.english: and Shmuel said: in the afternoon prayer.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָמַר: בְּמִנְחָה, וּשְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר: בִּתְפִלַּת הַמִּנְחָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives two competing answers to step 14's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב: in the afternoon. שמואל: during the מנחה prayer.

steps.title: רב יוסף supports שמואל from מגילת תענית
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף says שמואל's view makes sense, based on a line in מגילת תענית using the word ייסר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: it makes sense to follow שמואל, because it is written in מגילת תענית: 'Therefore, any person who took it upon himself beforehand will be bound.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף brings a source to back up שמואל: a line from מגילת תענית that ends with the word ייסר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מגילת תענית is a list of days when one may not fast. The line says that someone who took a fast on himself beforehand 'ייסר'. רב יוסף sees in that word a hint to accepting the fast at prayer. The next step spells out how.

keyTerms.meaning: Like him, in agreement with him
An early list of days when fasting is not allowed

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
It makes sense to rule like Shmuel,
as it is written in Megillat Ta'anit:
Therefore, any person
who takes it upon himself beforehand —
will be bound.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: כְּווֹתֵיהּ דִּשְׁמוּאֵל מִסְתַּבְּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to decide the argument in step 15 in favor of שמואל.
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's view that a fast is accepted during the מנחה prayer
steps.raayaSupportSource: The line in מגילת תענית ending with ייסר

steps.title: How the word ייסר proves שמואל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the proof: ייסר means he binds himself in his prayer.
steps.simpleTranslation: Doesn't it mean: he binds himself in his prayer?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how רב יוסף's proof works. ייסר is read as 'he binds himself in his prayer'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the binding happens 'in his prayer', then a fast is accepted during the מנחה prayer, exactly like שמואל said. This reading turns the word into support for שמואל against רב.

phrases.english: Doesn't it mean —
he binds himself in his prayer?
phrases.notes: בִּצְלוֹ comes from צְלוֹתָא, prayer, so this points to accepting the fast at מנחה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the logic behind רב יוסף's proof.
steps.raayaObject: Acceptance of a fast happens during prayer (שמואל)
steps.raayaSupportSource: Reading ייסר as 'binds himself in his prayer'

steps.title: No, read it as יאסר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof: the word should be read יאסר, 'he makes himself forbidden', which has nothing to do with prayer.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. It means: he makes himself forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away רב יוסף's proof by reading the word slightly differently, as יאסר, 'forbidden'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By swapping one letter, ייסר ('bound') becomes יאסר ('forbidden'). Then the line in מגילת תענית is saying that someone who took a fast on himself beforehand is forbidden to eat, so he keeps his fast even on those special days. It says nothing about prayer or about when a fast is accepted, so the proof for שמואל falls away.
steps.confusionAlert: ייסר and יאסר look almost the same. The only difference is the letter א, but the meaning changes from 'bound' to 'forbidden'.

phrases.english: No — he makes himself forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in steps 16-17.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof from מגילת תענית is rejected. שמואל's view itself is not disproved.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The word can be read as יאסר ('forbidden'), which says nothing about prayer or about when a fast is accepted.

steps.title: Two sages argue about the reading
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא and רבי שמעון ברבי argue about the word: one reads ייסר and the other reads יאסר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא and רבי שמעון ברבי argue about this. One said: ייסר. The other said: יאסר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports that the two readings just suggested are a real argument between רבי חייא and רבי שמעון ברבי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question of 'bound' versus 'forbidden' was not just raised to push away a proof. Earlier sages actually argued about which reading is correct, and the גמרא names them without saying who held which view.

phrases.english: They argue about it:
Rabbi Ḥiyya and Rabbi Shimon, son of Rabbi.
One said: 'He will be bound,'
and the other said: 'He will be forbidden.'

steps.triggerLanguage: פְּלִיגִי בַּהּ רַבִּי חִיָּיא וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בְּרַבִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the two readings from steps 17-18 match a real argument between earlier sages.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי חייא and רבי שמעון ברבי argue whether the text of מגילת תענית says ייסר or יאסר.

steps.title: What does the יאסר reading mean?
steps.stepSummary: The ייסר reading was explained already. The גמרא asks what the יאסר reading means.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who said ייסר means it as we explained. But according to the one who said יאסר, what does it mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says the 'bound' reading is clear from what was just said, and asks how to explain the 'forbidden' reading. It is setting up an explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ייסר was already explained as binding oneself in prayer. The גמרא now wants to know exactly what יאסר means in the context of מגילת תענית. The next step answers this.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it? What does it mean?

phrases.english: The one who said 'he will be bound' — it is as we said.
phrases.notes: This points back to step 17: binding oneself in prayer.

phrases.english: According to the one who said 'he will be forbidden' — what does it mean?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows up on the argument in step 19 by asking how to understand the second reading.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What does the reading יאסר mean in מגילת תענית?

steps.title: The meaning of יאסר: an earlier vow to fast still stands
steps.stepSummary: The יאסר reading means that a person who took on a fast before the rabbis made the festive days is forbidden to eat. An earlier vow overrides the decree, and an earlier decree overrides the vow.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught in מגילת תענית: Anyone who took a fast on himself beforehand is forbidden to eat. How so? Someone accepted on himself to fast every Monday, Thursday and Monday all year, and festive days from מגילת תענית fell on those days. If his vow came first, his vow cancels our decree. If our decree came first, our decree cancels his vow.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 20 by quoting the full passage from מגילת תענית that uses the word יאסר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here יאסר simply means 'he is forbidden to eat', so he must keep his fast. It has nothing to do with prayer. The rule depends on timing: whichever came first, the private vow or the rabbis' decree, wins.

keyTerms.meaning: An early list of happy days on which fasting is not allowed
Our decree, meaning the rabbis' decree setting up the festive days

steps.whatToRemember: Under the יאסר reading, a fasting vow made before the festive days were set up still requires the person to fast. A vow made after them does not take effect on those days.

phrases.english: As it is taught in מגילת תענית:
Any person who takes upon himself
beforehand will be forbidden.
phrases.notes: This is the יאסר reading from step 19. He is forbidden to eat, so he keeps his fast.

phrases.english: How so?
An individual who accepted upon himself
to fast Monday, Thursday and Monday
of the entire year,
and festive days fell on them
that are written in מגילת תענית,
if his vow came before our decree,
his vow cancels our decree,
and if our decree came before his vow,
our decree cancels his vow.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 20
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: יאסר means he is forbidden to eat. An earlier vow overrides the decree, and an earlier decree overrides the vow.

steps.title: Until when may one eat the night before a fast
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא records a dispute. רבי says one may eat until dawn, and רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון says until the rooster calls.
steps.simpleTranslation: The rabbis taught: Until when may one eat and drink? Until dawn rises. These are the words of רבי. רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון says: Until the rooster calls.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic with a ברייתא about how late at night one may still eat before a fast that begins in the morning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי allows eating all the way until dawn. רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון sets an earlier cutoff, the rooster's call, which comes before dawn.

keyTerms.meaning: Dawn, the first light of morning

phrases.aramaic: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: עַד מָתַי אוֹכֵל וְשׁוֹתֶה —
phrases.english: The rabbis taught: Until when may one eat and drink?
Until dawn rises,
the words of רבי.
רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון says:
Until the rooster calls.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: עַד מָתַי אוֹכֵל וְשׁוֹתֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new topic
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Eating is allowed until dawn (רבי) or until the rooster calls (רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון).

steps.title: אביי: only if he has not finished his meal
steps.stepSummary: אביי limits the ברייתא. One may keep eating only if he has not finished his meal. Once he finishes, he may not eat again.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: They taught this only when he has not finished his meal. But if he finished his meal, he may not eat.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי narrows the ruling of the ברייתא, saying when it applies and when it does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to אביי, eating through the night is allowed only as one continuous meal. Finishing the meal counts as ending his eating for the night.

keyTerms.meaning: They taught this only (in this case)

phrases.english: אביי said: They taught this only
when he has not finished his meal,
but if he finished his meal, he may not eat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the ברייתא of step 22
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After finishing his meal, a person may not eat again before the fast.

steps.title: רבא challenges: finished and stood up, yet he may eat
steps.stepSummary: רבא quotes a ברייתא that says someone who finished and stood up may still eat, against אביי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא challenged him: If he finished and stood up, he may eat!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא brings a ברייתא that seems to go directly against אביי's limit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says that even after finishing and getting up, a person may still eat. That seems to show that finishing the meal does not end his eating, which is the opposite of what אביי said.

phrases.english: רבא challenged him:
If he finished and stood up, he may eat!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks אביי's limit from step 23
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's rule that one who finished his meal may not eat
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא explicitly allows eating after finishing and standing up.

steps.title: The table was not yet cleared
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא is talking about someone who had not yet cleared away the table, so his meal is not really over.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, it is when he did not clear the table.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי's position is defended by explaining the ברייתא as a special case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: As long as the table has not been cleared, the meal is still considered going on, even if he stood up. So the ברייתא does not go against אביי.

phrases.english: There, it is when he did not clear away.
phrases.notes: He means he had not cleared the table yet, so the meal still counts as going on.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's challenge
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the source to a specific case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא allows eating even after the meal has truly ended.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is talking about a meal whose table was not yet cleared, so the meal is not over.

steps.title: Second version, רבא: only if he has not slept
steps.stepSummary: In another version, רבא limits the ברייתא. One may eat only if he has not slept. Once he has slept, he may not eat.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: רבא said: They taught this only when he did not sleep. But if he slept, he may not eat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of the discussion, in which רבא sets the limit at sleeping.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version, finishing the meal does not matter. Going to sleep is what ends a person's eating for the night.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new argument after the first one. It is a different version of the same discussion, with the roles of אביי and רבא switched and with sleep as the cutoff.

phrases.english: Some say: רבא said:
They taught this only when he did not sleep,
but if he slept, he may not eat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second version of the limit on the ברייתא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After sleeping, a person may not eat again before the fast.

steps.title: אביי challenges: slept and got up, yet he may eat
steps.stepSummary: אביי quotes a ברייתא that says someone who slept and got up may still eat, against רבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי challenged him: If he slept and got up, he may eat!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי brings a ברייתא that seems to contradict רבא's limit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא allows eating even after sleeping, which seems to directly reject רבא's rule.

phrases.english: אביי challenged him:
If he slept and got up, he may eat!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבא's limit from step 26
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's rule that one who slept may not eat
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא explicitly allows eating after sleeping and getting up.

steps.title: He was only dozing
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא is talking about someone who was only dozing, not truly asleep.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, it is someone who was dozing.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers that the ברייתא is about light dozing, which does not count as sleep.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only real sleep ends a person's eating for the night. A light doze does not, so the ברייתא fits with רבא's rule.

phrases.english: There, it is someone who was dozing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the source to a specific case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא allows eating even after real sleep.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is talking about light dozing, not real sleep.

steps.title: What counts as dozing?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for a definition of dozing, and רב אשי begins to answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case of dozing? רב אשי said:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what exactly counts as dozing. It is setting up רב אשי's definition, which comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer in step 28 depends on telling dozing apart from real sleep, so the גמרא needs a clear test. Only the opening words of רב אשי's answer appear here.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? How does it look?

phrases.english: What is the case of dozing?
רב אשי said:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for a definition of the term used in step 28
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A definition of dozing, as opposed to real sleep.
